mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved by 5.2 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w, signaling a consistent upward trend. This momentum will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC higher than the prior four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -79.6 to -74.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below or equal to the mean of the prior 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen 9.9 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w. As workplace attendance recovers, commuting patterns stabilize and weekday retail visitation increases proportionally, lifting four-week RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 8 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES declines or stagnates in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite WORKPLACES gains.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 23.3 to 19.4 percentage points above baseline, indicating people are spending less time at home. This behavioral shift toward out-of-home activity will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 23.3 to 19.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 22 percentage points, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite RESIDENTIAL decline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved 7.4 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w. Increased transit use signals restored commuting and mobility infrastructure utilization, which enables retail foot traffic recovery over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 5 percentage points over two weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT declines in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not show improvement within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has improved 14.1 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w, and GROCERY_PHARM has improved 7.1 percentage points. Joint recovery in outdoor and essential retail signals broad mobility normalization that will lift discretionary RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM rise more than 5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: Either PARKS or GROCERY_PHARM declines in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite both proxies rising.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has remained severely depressed at -66.9 percent. If TRANSIT does not recover above -50 percent within two weeks, it signals persistent mobility restrictions that will constrain RETAIL_REC growth, keeping it below the prior four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -50 percent in week t+1w
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -50 percent within one week, or RETAIL_REC increases despite TRANSIT stagnation.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL show opposing trends: WORKPLACES rising while RESIDENTIAL falls. This divergence indicates a shift from home-based to workplace-based activity. However, if WORKPLACES gains do not exceed 10 percentage points over the next two weeks, the behavioral shift will be insufficient to overcome retail suppression, keeping RETAIL_REC flat or declining.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises less than 10 percentage points over two weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains below 20
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises more than 10 percentage points in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases despite weak WORKPLACES momentum.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has improved only 7.1 percentage points over four weeks, remaining at -32.0 percent. Weak essential retail recovery signals constrained household purchasing power and mobility capacity. This constraint will limit discretionary RETAIL_REC growth to below the prior four-week mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains below -30 percent in t+0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -25 percent within one week, or RETAIL_REC increases more than 5 percentage points despite weak GROCERY_PHARM recovery.
